answers.reason: The chancellor heads the central administration and is involved in university-wide planning and leadership matters.
The chancellor is responsible for the budget and staff, making participation in the budget planning round central to their office.
Appointment decisions touch upon university-wide plans and funding, involving office holders of higher rank like the chancellor.
Faculty councils decide on affairs of individual faculties, which are separate from the central administration headed by the chancellor.
Study commissions deal with faculty teaching and degree programmes rather than central budgetary or administrative leadership.
Examination boards decide on individual student examination matters within faculties, not central administration.
Internal research funding rounds are faculty-level grant processes outside the direct remit of the central administration head.
Rewriting module descriptions is a faculty-level degree programme task.
Laboratory equipment procurement is managed within specific faculty teaching units.
Orientation week planning is an organizational task for new students at the faculty or student level.
